correctness.rationale: The finite claim is reduced to exact recurrences derived from the published Schemmel formula. A deterministic linear sieve provides every least prime factor through 100000000. Because L_2(n)<n for n>1, D_2(n)=L_2(n)+D_2(L_2(n)) is evaluated only from previously computed exact integers. The finalized verifier scans the entire domain and asserts that its fixed-point vector is exactly [37147,53290831], while also checking the exact prime count 5761455.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies the existence and distribution of D_m-perfect numbers as a natural open direction. An exact 100000000 cutoff extends the paper's stated 100000 computation by three decimal orders and, unlike that original range, lies beyond the second known fixed point 53290831. It therefore establishes a natural finite classification rather than an arbitrary sample or a recomputation of a known table.
